title: Are there dead bodies on Mount Everest?
summary: Josh and Chuck open with a shameless plug for their spoken word economics album, then turn to whether dead bodies remain on Mount Everest. They discuss Everest's height and climbing season, the death zone, the roughly 89 deaths and bodies left on the mountain, George Mallory's remains and the Hillary/Tenzing summit question, Sherpa roles, Ian Woodall and Francis Arsentiev's abandonment, Into Thin Air, trash on the mountain, and the difficulty of retrieving bodies. The episode closes with blog updates, a cartoon of the hosts, and listener mail about the game MDK.

segments.title: Opening and spoken word album plug
segments.summary: The hosts open and plug their spoken word economics album, the Super Stuff Guide to the Economy, available for purchase.

segments.title: Mountaineering experience and shift to Everest
segments.summary: Chuck describes his hiking and mountain experience, and the hosts introduce Into Thin Air and Jon Krakauer's book about a deadly 1996 Everest expedition, along with Into the Wild.

segments.title: Everest facts: height, location, and weather
segments.summary: The hosts give Everest's height of 29,035 feet (8,850 meters), note it sits on the Nepal-Tibet border, and describe the May and June climbing windows, the jet stream, and extreme winds and cold.

segments.title: Death counts and bodies left on the mountain
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the number of deaths on Everest (about 89 at the time of the article), summit counts, why bodies usually stay in the death zone, and why bringing bodies down is considered very dangerous.

segments.title: George Mallory, Hillary and Tenzing summit debate
segments.summary: The hosts discuss George Mallory's frozen body found below the summit and whether he reached the top before Hillary and Tenzing Norgay, who are credited with the first documented summit.

segments.title: Sherpas, abandoned climbers, and Ian Woodall
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the role of Sherpas, the 2006 death of John Sharp, climbers passing dying people, Hillary's criticism, and Ian Woodall's controversial role in the Krakauer expedition and abandoning Francis Arsentiev.

segments.title: Trash and the future of Everest
segments.summary: The hosts note the roughly 120 tons of trash left on Everest each year, Chinese cleanup expeditions, and a hopeful outlook on technology and changing attitudes toward rescue.

segments.title: Blog update and cartoon
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh promote the show blog, weekly podcast recaps, and a comic strip by Greg Williams about the junk mail episode.

segments.title: Listener mail: corrections and MDK game
segments.summary: The hosts read a correction coup from Jonathan Pesky and clarify that the game listeners described is MDK, not MK Ultra.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners and sign off, asking for mail at the show's address.
